case.title: Records vault entry during a busy shift
case.objective: Establish why Jordan Pell entered Records Vault B-12 at 14:07 on 12 March 2026, whether the entry had an assigned task, and why the vault door was held open from 14:09 to 14:12.
case.setting: Interview room 2, Office of Facility Security, Halvern Street Annex. The subject attends during work hours; the interview is administrative and voluntary.

initial_documents.title: Access exception report, Records Vault B-12, 12 March 2026

content.body: Generated 16:00 by the end-of-day roster check (O. Varga, Records Vault Custodian). Exception: B-12 is not on J. Pell's daily task roster. Badge 30418 last opened B-12 on 19 November 2025. No other B-12 badge entries on 12 March. The B-12 exit does not require a badge, so no exit time is recorded.

initial_documents.title: Records Vault B-12 access rules (Facility Security Standard 4.2)

content.body: Entry to B-12 requires an assigned task: an open work order or a supervisor dispatch recorded on the radio log. Staff must not hold the vault door open longer than 60 seconds except while moving equipment, and must stay at the open door. Sealed records boxes may be opened only by the custodian or under a signed custodian release.
Supervisor on duty: I. Marrow. Scheduled technicians: J. Pell, D. Rusk, K. Okafor-Lyle, S. Tamsin. Absent: D. Rusk (sick leave), S. Tamsin (training). Technicians on shift: J. Pell, K. Okafor-Lyle.

data.title: Records Vault B-12 seal audit, 12 March 2026

content.body: Audit by O. Varga at 16:10. 214 sealed boxes checked; 213 match the register. Box ACQ-117 (Annex parking-lot resurfacing, bid evaluations): registered seal #55102, found seal #55419. Seal supply drawer log: seal #55419 removed at 14:15, no initials, no custodian release on file.

data.text: The end-of-day seal audit checked the sealed boxes in B-12 against the seal register and the seal supply drawer log. Did you handle any records boxes, seals or the seal drawer while you were in the vault?
I was just focusing on the sensors while I was in the vault, so I didn't have any reason to be handling boxes or the supply drawer.

question.assessment: The investigator directly presents the seal audit findings regarding box ACQ-117 and the seal supply drawer log.

flags.quote: I was just focusing on the sensors while I was in the vault, so I didn't have any reason to be handling boxes or the supply drawer.
flags.conflict_record_quote: Box ACQ-117: registered seal #55102, found seal #55419. Seal supply drawer log: seal #55419 removed at 14:15, no initials, no custodian release on file.

follow_up.question: How did seal number 55419 come to be used on box ACQ-117 during your time in the vault?
follow_up.purpose: Ask the subject to explain the direct contradiction between their denial of handling boxes or seals and the physical seal audit finding.

finding.label: deceptive
corroboration_needed: verify B-12 security camera footage if available
finding.rationale: The subject entered B-12 without authorization, held the door open for three minutes, and explicitly denied handling any boxes or the seal supply drawer, which directly contradicts the post-audit finding that seal #55419 was removed and placed on box ACQ-117 during the access window.

outcome.resolution: Marrow radioed Pell to a humidity alarm in Room B-10. He reset it, reported 'B-10 done' at 14:05, then used his Environmental Response access to enter Records Vault B-12 at 14:07 with no task there. He broke the seal on box ACQ-117 and read the bid evaluations for a contract his cousin's firm is bidding on, propped the door so he could hear anyone approaching, and resealed the box with a supply-drawer seal at 14:15. Distractors shared with the truthful variant: the late work order, the short-staffed shift and the supervisor not remembering the room.
